stable_polymorph: rock-salt CoO (paramagnetic NaCl type; tetragonal AFM distortion below ~290 K)
evidence_type: calorimetry: zinc blende 37 +/- 10 kJ/mol above rock salt (DiCarlo & Navrotsky 1993, abstract; PDF requested)
reason: Measured: DiCarlo & Navrotsky 1993 (J. Am. Ceram. Soc. 76:2465) find zinc-blende CoO 37 +/- 10 kJ/mol (about 190 meV/atom) less stable than rock salt, consistent with a 38 kJ/mol lattice-energy estimate. Zinc blende converts to rock salt on heating near 310-320 C (Risbud 2005 p.835). MP puts rock salt 92 meV/atom above zinc blende, so its error here is about 280 meV/atom.

evidence_type: cited heat-capacity anomaly (transition not in the assessment)
reason: Grundy 2003 leaves the alpha-beta transition out of the assessment and cites a lambda Cp peak at 307.5 K (Robie & Hemingway): orthorhombic alpha is the 298 K form, cubic beta (Ia-3) above about 300 K, only about 10 K away.

Pyrolusite is the stable MnO2; all other MnO2 modifications are called metastable. Fritsch 1998 (Table 5 p.478; p.477) could measure no cation-free hollandite, so MP I4/m is not the ground state. MP Pnnm entry not checked against rutile.

evidence_type: conversion on heating to the denser phase; no calorimetry found; all published DFT agree
reason: No measured enthalpy of the bixbyite-corundum conversion was found. Bixbyite V2O3 converts to corundum near 823 K in inert gas (Weber 2011 p.6766). Corundum is about 9% denser, so it is the lower-entropy form; a conversion on heating toward it must be driven by enthalpy, which then favors corundum at lower T too. Published DFT puts bixbyite about 9 kJ/mol per formula unit (about 19 meV/atom) above corundum (Weber 2011; Wessel 2012, J. Comput. Chem., doi 10.1002/jcc.23046, unverified in full text). MP puts bixbyite 8.7 meV/atom below. Verdict inferred, not measured.

stable_polymorph: V3O5 (monoclinic; low- and high-T forms not distinguished)
reason: Kang treats one monoclinic V3O5 line compound and names no space group. Both MP entries (P2/c, C2/c) are monoclinic, so this source does not decide between them.
Orthorhombic V2O5 is the only V2O5 phase of the assessed 1-bar diagram; the competing MP C2/c (delta) is monoclinic.

One 1-bar Ti2O3 line compound with a low-T modification to 470 K (transition 1138 J/mol, SGTE). The paper never names the structure, so it cannot place R-3c against Pnma; the corundum identity would come from outside this source.

Bulk monoclinic -> tetragonal +10.61 +/- 0.57 kJ/mol at 25 C (oxide-melt calorimetry). Wang 2006 abstract p.3751: m <-> t T0 = 1367 +/- 5 K by DTA, monoclinic P21/c at low T. Cubic Fm-3m only at high T.

locus: Abstract p.4675; Sec. 3.2.2 p.4677; Table 5 p.4678
reason: Thorite -> huttonite +6.7 +/- 2.5 kJ/mol (drop solution); thorite -> huttonite on heating at 1210 C (cited). Both polymorphs are metastable in enthalpy vs ThO2 + quartz at 298 K (+19.6 and +26.3 kJ/mol, Table 5).
C stable from 298 K to C <-> H at 2600 +/- 30 K (recommended); no C-B transition at 1 bar for Y2O3. Kapush 2017 p.207: C -> H 43 +/- 4 kJ/mol. B (C2/m) is a high-pressure form.

A stable to A <-> H at 2313 +/- 20 K; the low-T C form of La2O3 is tied to volatile impurities, not a polymorph. Konings 2014 Sec. 3.1.1 p.013101-9: A at room temperature. Ushakov 2011 p.845: A -> H 23 +/- 5 kJ/mol at 2046 C.
A at room temperature, A -> H selected 2392 +/- 30 K. Zinkevich 2007 Sec. 5.3 p.616: C and B are unstable vs A at any temperature for La-Nd; Table 2.2 A <-> H 2338 +/- 60 K.

Calorimetric C -> A is 0.0 +/- 0.3 kJ/mol at 298 K, so enthalpy alone does not separate them; the assessment (positive transition entropy) and Konings 2014 Sec. 3.6.1 p.013101-15 put A stable at room temperature.

stable_polymorph: disputed: A-type (Zinkevich) or C-type to ~900 K (Konings)
reason: Zinkevich: A stable at all T, C only with impurities, and he rejects the calorimetric C -> A +24.5 +/- 4.2 kJ/mol (which would favour C). Konings: C probably stable from room temperature to 873-923 K. The reviews disagree.
C is "probably" stable at room temperature; B above ~1073 K but the transition was reported irreversible. Zinkevich 2007 p.601 calls the Pm2O3 values very uncertain. Not settled.

locus: Sec. 1 p.601; Table 2.2 p.604; Table 5.1 p.614
reason: C -> B +3.8 +/- 2.6 kJ/mol (Konings 2014 p.013101-19: 3.8 +/- 6.2 from the dHf of both forms). C <-> B only estimated (676 +/- 20 K, category E); both reviews call low-T C stability debated or probable.

evidence_type: equilibrium oxygen potentials of both forms; calorimetry
reason: C is the stable form at standard conditions; C <-> B 1350 +/- 15 K from the crossing of measured oxygen potentials of both forms; C -> B +12.1 +/- 6.0 kJ/mol at 298 K (Zinkevich Table 5.1). Zinkevich estimates 894 K for C <-> B but also has C at 298 K. Konings prints C-type as 'fluorite-type, Fm-3m', a misprint for bixbyite Ia-3.

evidence_type: critical review; reversible C <-> B; calorimetry
reason: C (Ia-3) at room temperature; C <-> B sluggish but reversible, selected 1473 K. Zinkevich Table 5.1 p.614: C -> B +5.3 +/- 0.4 kJ/mol at 1561 K (calorimetric).
C at room temperature to C -> B at 1823 +/- 30 K (Zinkevich Table 2.2: 1823 +/- 50 K, probable). B (C2/m) only above that or under pressure.
C to C -> B at 2538 +/- 30 K (Zinkevich Table 2.2: 2458 +/- 20 K, recommended, reversible).
C to C -> H at 2538 +/- 30 K (Zinkevich Table 2.2: 2593 +/- 50 K); no B at 1 bar.
Fcc Fm-3m PrO2, stable in O2 to 587-663 K, then decomposes to Pr6O11; no other PrO2 form at 1 bar. Pnma not discussed.

Berlinite is lowest in enthalpy of every dense and microporous AlPO4 measured (tridymite +5.12 +/- 1.38, cristobalite +6.09 +/- 1.16 kJ/mol at 298 K). MP GGA-lowest I-4 is not berlinite and matches no measured form.
Beta is stable at room temperature and transforms at 1125 C to alpha (P21/a, MP GGA-lowest), which is retained metastably. Xie 2004 p.1001: gamma (tuite, R-3m) is the high-pressure phase.
CA is a stable 1-bar compound of the assessment, but no structure is given, so P21/c against Pnma is not decided by this source.

stable_polymorph: none (C4A3 is not a stable 1-bar compound)
reason: Stable intermediate phases are C3A, C12A7, CA, CA2 and CA6 only, so neither MP polymorph is a ground state at this composition.

stable_polymorph: alpha-LiAlO2 below 1023 K in the assessment (identity ambiguous)
locus: Table I p.2918; Sec. B.1 p.2932
reason: Assessment places alpha below 1023 K and gamma above (heating data 848-1173 K, dilatometry and DTA), against the provisional call. Its Table I lists alpha as cubic I4132, not R-3m, so alpha is not tied to MP R-3m here.
One NaAlO2 phase (Cp from Barin), no polymorphs or structure, so it does not decide Pna21 against R-3m.

stable_polymorph: cubic spinel at room temperature (XRD only)
reason: Calorimetry covers only cubic Li1+xMn2-xO4; the low-T orthorhombic form is not measured, so the ranking against MP Fddd is not settled.

Opx-cpx-ilm triple point at 0.98 GPa and 752 K; cpx-ilm boundary reaches 0 GPa at 600 K; ilmenite stable at ambient, opx stable at 1 bar from ~900 to 1828 K. MP GGA-lowest C2/c (cpx) is not stable at ambient. Provisional named opx.

Pyroxenoid -> garnet +0.50 +/- 2.55 and garnet -> ilmenite +8.79 +/- 3.35 kJ/mol (sum 9.29), ilmenite a high-pressure phase; MP is right that R-3 is not the ground state, but the pyroxenoid structure is undetermined, so C2/c cannot be matched.
Single-crystal P21/c structure; AgO itself is metastable (decomposes exothermically to Ag2O + O2). No polymorph energetics.
Hydrothermal ilmenite NaNbO3 converts irreversibly and exothermically to perovskite at ~485 C; no enthalpy magnitude or 298 K ranking. MP denser Pna21 is not the room-temperature P phase either.
Hexagonal LuFeO3 from containerless processing is called metastable and converts irreversibly to orthorhombic above ~1273 K (cited); no thermodynamic measurement.
Beta-BaB4O7 is made at high pressure; on heating at 1 bar it goes X-ray amorphous at 800-850 C rather than back to alpha. Only DFT ranks the enthalpies.
Hydrothermal zircon-type LaVO4 is unchanged after 2 h at 500 C and monazite after 2 h at 600 C; monazite is called the equilibrium form, but there is no thermodynamic measurement.

This is a high-pressure structure review with no calorimetry or reversed equilibria, so it is consistent with MP but does not establish the 298 K ground state.
